reading.body:
Emailage is not a data center: it was a fraud-scoring software company that ran on rented cloud capacity, and its old address now holds a different tenant. It adds zero megawatts to Arizona's total.

The point is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a data center. The company it names built analytics software that scored transaction risk by email address for online merchants and financial institutions. It consumed cloud and outsourced infrastructure rather than operating colocation or hosting of its own. A reverse geocode of the stored coordinates now resolves to Safe T Professionals LLC at 25 South Arizona Place in Chandler, which indicates the building changed hands after the point was tagged. The address sits several miles from the other eight rows in its batch, so no shared building connects them.

This matters because facility counts feed directly into claims about AI scaling. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities and only 4 with published capacity figures, totaling 512 MW. A mistagged software office inflates the first number without touching the second. The difference between a company that buys compute and one that supplies it is the entire distinction the category is meant to capture.

What the data does not cover is how common the error is. No published specifications exist for this location, and no source ties the Chandler address to server or hosting infrastructure. The 512 MW figure counts only facilities that publish capacity, so it is a floor rather than a full measure of Arizona's power draw. Correcting one point says nothing about how many other entries carry the same mistag.
